claim: RLS does not gate TRUNCATE, so the Supabase default ACL on schema public let the public anon key empty any future table there regardless of policies.

method.probe_table: public._priv_probe_0060 — created exactly like any new table, RLS enabled, 0 policies (maximum protection a table can have), 3 rows inserted
method.probe_view: public._priv_probe_0060_v — plain view over the probe table
method.actor: set local role anon inside a DO block; each verb wrapped in its own exception handler; result raised so the transaction rolls back and nothing is left behind
method.cleanup: both probe objects dropped after each pass; verified absent

before.anon_delete: ok, rows_deleted=0 — RLS blocked it, the protection worked

scope.affects: objects created in schema public from now on
scope.does_not_affect: every existing table and view — pg_default_acl is not retroactive, so no live system changes behaviour
